what: Indexed samples (Sailor, 2026-10-16). An index is a fixed basket of publications — one or more per corner — swept on the same object in the same window, every day. The composite per corner is the index value for the day; join the four and you get the day's figure. Opportunistic cuts show who happened to speak; an index shows what the same four readers said. Balance is by design, not by luck.
rules: members are fixed; a change to the basket is a new index version, dated
every member is swept every day it publishes (the sweep is mechanical: headlines · deks · openings · transcripts); only pieces that touch the index's object are cut
beta ledes (headline · dek · opening of a paywalled piece) run as data: they print on the paper flagged, and do NOT enter the index composite until the member is subscribed and read in full
the floor is a separate series: an index member may also be the floor (The Close), but the floor is never computed from the index — a yardstick that changes length isn't a yardstick
an index reads one object at a time; the same basket may run on several objects as separate indices
